In the `backend-quality` container, PostgreSQL is exposed through the `postgres` service hostname, but this step supplies no database environment variables. `scripts/test-course-identity.sh` consequently defaults `PGHOST` to `127.0.0.1`, while `PGUSER` and `PGPASSWORD` are also unset, so its initial `createdb` cannot connect and every backend CI run that reaches this added step fails. Pass the same `PGHOST`, `PGUSER`, and `PGPASSWORD` values used by the two preceding PostgreSQL tests.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Unify idempotency across the checkout feature branch**

When a retry crosses a change to the production `commerce.courses` flag, the same key is handled by two independent stores: the disabled branch records it in `identity_course_registration_request`, while the enabled branch only checks `course_registration_checkout_runtime`. A fallback registration accepted before enablement can therefore be retried afterward to create a second registration and seat hold; the reverse transition can turn an accepted checkout retry into a duplicate lead and return no checkout details. Check both stores before selecting the branch, or use one route-level idempotency record that preserves the original outcome across flag changes.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the receipt key constraint with API validation**

Public registration validates keys with `ServiceStorefront.validateIdempotencyKey`, which accepts every visible ASCII character, but this constraint permits only letters, digits, `_`, and `-`. Thus a valid 16–128 character caller key containing common punctuation such as `.` or `:` passes request validation and then fails this insert with a PostgreSQL constraint exception, producing a server error instead of a registration. Use the same length/visible-ASCII contract in both layers, or reject the narrower character set before entering the transaction.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep unverified contacts out of primary identity fields**

When an existing account holder submits a course enquiry—or two legitimate attendees share an email as this change explicitly permits—this creates multiple `Party` rows with the same primary email/phone. Other production flows such as `ensurePartyRecordDb`, `ensurePartyWithAccount`, and `ensurePartyForInquiry` resolve those fields through `selectUniquePartyByPrimaryEmail`/`selectUniquePartyByPrimaryPhone`, which return 409 when more than one row matches; for example, the affected customer can no longer complete public service booking at `createPublicBookingCheckout`'s `ensurePartyRecord` call. Store these unverified course details outside the shared primary identity fields, or exclude source-scoped course contacts from those identity selectors.

When this commit is passed to the guarded production release, the release is rejected because `9bc040b7...` is not an ancestor of `ccc0a5ae...` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1). The check in `scripts/production-release.mjs` explicitly refuses every manifest entry whose `introducedBy` commit is outside the release SHA's ancestry, so this migration cannot be deployed from the reviewed commit; preserve the actual introduction commit in this history or otherwise make the manifest reference a valid introduction ancestor.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope confirmation throttling to each registration**

When two legitimate attendees register with the same email within 24 hours—a case this change now explicitly permits—this invokes `sendConfirmation` for both, but `courseEmailSentWithinLast24Hours` searches only by recipient email and marks the second confirmation as skipped. The second registration therefore succeeds without receiving its own acknowledgement; include the registration ID in the throttle lookup or otherwise allow one confirmation per distinct registration while still suppressing retries.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Confirmation lookup now includes the registration ID and registration_confirmation event type, so another attendee using the same email does not suppress this acknowledgement. Accepted request retries still return before sending. Added a PostgreSQL regression that seeds a sent confirmation for one shared-email registration, verifies the other remains eligible, and verifies replay adds no email event. Hosted validation is running; this change will be included in the combined final release.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep unverified contacts out of primary identity fields**

Fresh evidence in this exact SHA contradicts the earlier resolution: course contacts are still written to `PartyPrimaryEmail`/`PartyPrimaryPhone`, while `ensurePartyWithAccount` and `ensurePartyForInquiry` still call `selectUniquePartyByPrimaryEmail`/`selectUniquePartyByPrimaryPhone`, whose shared selector returns 409 for multiple matches. Because this change deliberately permits separate attendees to share an email, two registrations can therefore make later account creation or ad-inquiry submission fail for that address; store the unverified values outside the primary identity fields or exclude these source-scoped contacts from identity selection.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retry confirmations after transient delivery failures**

When SMTP delivery fails transiently, `sendConfirmation` catches the exception and records a failed event, but the receipt and registration have already committed; a retry with the same idempotency key resolves that receipt with `created = False`, so this guard permanently skips another delivery attempt. Previously, retrying a pending registration invoked confirmation again, and the existing sent-event check already prevents duplicates. Allow retries when no successful confirmation exists rather than conditioning all delivery on first creation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

body: Keeping automatic delivery limited to the first accepted source operation is intentional. A caught SMTP exception is not proof that the recipient server rejected the message: delivery can succeed before the acknowledgement is lost. Retrying whenever no sent event exists can therefore send duplicates, contrary to the task’s explicit retry invariant. The accepted registration and failed course_email_event remain available in the authorized registration dossier’s email history. Uncertain delivery needs operator review; public request retries must not blindly redispatch. Automatic recovery would need provider idempotency or a proven pre-acceptance failure classification. This limitation is documented rather than claiming delivery succeeded.
